title: Compass and Provision
premise: Hazel Marchetti flies medicine and gossip into the mountain interior, paying off her late father's debts one cargo run at a time. When her old rival, Silas Crane, hires her crew to retrieve a downed supply plane before the snows seal the range, she discovers the wreck holds the deed and ledgers that could free her father's name — or hang his old partners. Betrayed by the man who hired her and sheltered by the found family of her airstrip town, Hazel must choose between reclaiming her legacy and protecting the people who became her own. In the end she burns the ledgers over the pass, keeps the compass, and lands home with something worth more than a debt forgiven.
about_author: Oscar Vasquez is a former bush mechanic turned storyteller who spent a decade hauling freight across northern ranges before trading wrenches for a keyboard. He writes adventure fiction from a cabin with an unreliable generator and a very reliable dog.

chapters.title: Fuel, Rumors, and Rain
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A routine med run into the interior establishes her world: the airstrip town of Kettle Creek, her ragtag crew, and the debt shadowing her father's memory. She overhears rumors of a wrecked plane high in the Sawtooth Range. Emotional beat: weary competence masking loneliness.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owes Her Nothing
chapters.summary: Silas Crane arrives unannounced, offering triple rates for a recovery flight before the snows. Hazel refuses; her mechanic, Junie, quietly accepts on the crew's behalf because winter wages are survival. Emotional beat: pride colliding with obligation, the first crack in Hazel's control.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with a flashback to the accident that killed her father and ended the last Crane expedition. She agrees to fly only as far as the base camp, swearing not to cross the pass. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing, guilt dressed up as caution.

chapters.title: Base Camp Lies
chapters.summary: At the glacier camp, Hazel finds Crane's manifest doesn't match his story — he's hunting documents, not salvage. Young deckhand Theo accidentally reveals Crane has her father's old flight logs. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into resolve; the crew begins choosing sides.

chapters.title: The Pass Closes Early
chapters.summary: A storm front traps the expedition above the pass with a dying prospector among them. Hazel must fly through weather she swore off to get him out — or watch him die. Emotional beat: duty versus self-preservation, and the first taste of what she's capable of.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Kept
chapters.summary: Crane reaches the wreck and recovers the ledgers proving Hazel's father was framed by his partners — partners who now bankroll Crane. He offers Hazel a share if she helps him sell the story. Emotional beat: temptation, vindication, and the sourness of power bought with betrayal.

chapters.title: Compass Points Home
chapters.summary: Junie and Theo arrive against orders, having discovered Crane plans to silence Hazel once the deal closes. The crew becomes a true family around a campfire, sharing what each lost. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing; love against duty takes shape as Hazel realizes the ledgers matter less than the people.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Crane takes the ledgers and Hazel's compass at gunpoint, stranding the crew as the storm peaks. Hazel navigates the escape on instinct and starlight alone, leading them across the icefield toward a hidden cache strip her father left. Emotional beat: terror transformed into fierce clarity.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Climax. At the cache strip, Hazel confronts Crane as he preps his plane. She offers him the truth instead of the ledgers — testimony that would ruin his backers too — and when he refuses, the storm and his own greed ground him permanently. She burns the ledgers in the stove. Emotional beat: power renounced, corruption left to consume itself.

chapters.title: Provision
chapters.summary: Resolution. Spring: Kettle Creek thrives as word of the burned ledgers spreads and the old partners' grip loosens. Hazel repaints her father's compass needle red and takes Junie and Theo on as partners in a new charter outfit. Emotional beat: quiet joy; the debt was never money, and it is finally paid.
